arxiv-1908-03260.title: De-anonymization Attacks on Neuroimaging Datasets
arxiv-1908-03260.creator: Vikram Ravindra, Ananth Grama
arxiv-1908-03260.description: Abstract Advances in imaging technologies, combined with inexpensive storage, have led to an explosion in the volume of publicly available neuroimaging datasets. Effective analyses of these images hold the potential for uncovering mechanisms that govern functioning of the human brain, and understanding various neurological diseases and disorders.

arxiv-2204-12422.title: Classical route to ergodicity and scarring phenomena in a two-component Bose-Josephson junction
arxiv-2204-12422.creator: Debabrata Mondal, Sudip Sinha, Sayak Ray, Johann Kroha, Subhasis Sinha
arxiv-2204-12422.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Debabrata Mondal, Sudip Sinha, Sayak Ray, Johann Kroha, Subhasis Sinha. We consider a Bose-Josephson junction (BJJ) formed by a binary mixture of ultracold atoms to investigate the manifestation of coherent collective dynamics on ergodicity and quantum scars , unfolding the connection between them. By tuning the inter- and intra-species interaction, we demonstrate a rich variety of Josephson dynamics and transitions between them, which plays a crucial role in controlling the overall ergodic behavior.

arxiv-2302-08383.title: On mixed radial Moore graphs of diameter 3 3
arxiv-2302-08383.creator: J.M. Ceresuela, N. López, D. Chemisana
arxiv-2302-08383.description: Abstract Radial Moore graphs and digraphs are extremal graphs related to the Moore ones where the distance-preserving spanning tree is preserved for some vertices. This leads to classify them according to their proximity to being a Moore graph or digraph.

arxiv-2304-14861.title: Scroll Waves and Filaments in excitable Media of higher spatial Dimension
arxiv-2304-14861.creator: Marie Cloet 1,2, Louise Arno 1,2, Desmond Kabus 1,3,2, Joeri Van der Veken 4, Alexander V. Panfilov 5,6,7, Hans Dierckx 1,2
arxiv-2304-14861.description: Abstract Excitable media are ubiquitous in nature, and in such systems the local excitation tends to self-organize in traveling waves, or in rotating spiral-shaped patterns in two or three spatial dimensions. Examples include waves during a pandemic or electrical scroll waves in the heart.

arxiv-2312-10925.title: Delving Deeper Into Astromorphic Transformers
arxiv-2312-10925.creator: Md Zesun Ahmed Mia, Malyaban Bal, Abhronil Sengupta
arxiv-2312-10925.description: Abstract Preliminary attempts at incorporating the critical role of astrocytes—cells that constitute more than 50% of human brain cells—in brain-inspired neuromorphic computing remain in infancy. This paper seeks to delve deeper into various key aspects of neuron-synapse-astrocyte interactions to mimic self-attention mechanisms in Transformers.

arxiv-2410-13239.title: On a relative dependency formula
arxiv-2410-13239.creator: Shashi Ranjan Sinha
arxiv-2410-13239.description: Abstract . Celikbas, Liang and Sadeghi established a one-sided inequality for the relative version of Jorgensen’s dependency formula and questioned whether it would be an equality. In this paper, we show that the inequality can be indeed strict, and prove a relative dependency formula.

arxiv-2506-01016.title: Optimistic critics can empower small actors
arxiv-2506-01016.creator: Olya Mastikhina, Dhruv Sreenivas, Pablo Samuel Castro
arxiv-2506-01016.description: Abstract Actor-critic methods have been central to many of the recent advances in deep reinforcement learning. The most common approach is to use symmetric architectures, whereby both actor and critic have the same network topology and number of parameters. However, recent works have argued for the advantages of asymmetric setups, specifically with the use of smaller actors.

arxiv-2511-06093.title: Magneto-Optical Study of Chiral Magnetic Modes in NiI 2 : Direct Evidence for Kitaev Interactions
arxiv-2511-06093.creator: Kartik Panda, Chaebin Kim, Daniel Bazyliansky, Javier Taboada-Gutiérrez, Florian Le Mardelé, Jan Dzian, Guy Levy, Jae Ha Kim, Youjin Lee, Bumchan Park, Martin Mourigal, Jae Hoon Kim, Alexey B. Kuzmenko, Milan Orlita, Je-Geun Park, Nimrod Bachar
arxiv-2511-06093.description: Abstract Bond-dependent magnetic interactions, particularly those described by the Kitaev model, have emerged as a key pathway toward realizing unconventional magnetic states such as quantum spin liquids and topologically nontrivial excitations, including skyrmions. These interactions frustrate conventional magnetic order and give rise to rich collective behavior that continues to challenge both theory and experiment.

hunter-blood-inflammation-1794.description: Hunter's posthumous masterpiece (1794): the physiology of blood and inflammation applied to surgery — the foundation of scientific surgery. First edition; bookseller's catalogue matter removed.

pmc-10583076.title: Hear my voice: understanding how community health workers in the Peruvian Amazon expanded their roles to mitigate the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic through community-based participatory research
pmc-10583076.creator: Tina Samsamshariat, Purnima Madhivanan, Alexandra Reyes Fernández Prada, Eva M Moya, Graciela Meza, Stefan Reinders, Magaly M Blas
pmc-10583076.description: IntroductionThe COVID-19 pandemic led to the collapse of the Peruvian health system, disrupting healthcare access for indigenous communities in the Amazon. Our study analysed how community health workers (CHWs) from indigenous communities in the Peruvian Amazon expanded their roles to mitigate the effects of the COVID-19 pandemic.

pmc-10682140.title: International Urogynecology consultation chapter 2 committee 3: the clinical evaluation of pelvic organ prolapse including investigations into associated morbidity/pelvic floor dysfunction
pmc-10682140.creator: Heather Barbier, Cassandra L Carberry, Päivi K Karjalainen, Charlotte K Mahoney, Valentín Manríquez Galán, Anna Rosamilia, Esther Ruess, David Shaker, Karishma Thariani
pmc-10682140.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Introduction and hypothesisThis manuscript from Chapter 2 of the International Urogynecology Consultation (IUC) on Pelvic Organ Prolapse (POP) reviews the literature involving the clinical evaluation of a patient with POP and associated bladder and bowel dysfunction.MethodsAn international group of 11 clinicians performed a search of the literature using pre-specified search MESH terms in PubMed and Embase databases (January 2000 to August 2020). Publications were eliminated if not relevant to the clinical evaluation of patients or did not include clear definitions of POP.

pmc-11375557.title: Research progress of epithelial-mesenchymal transformation-related transcription factors in peritoneal metastases
pmc-11375557.creator: Lei Wang, Xiaobei Peng, Chang Ma, Lin Hu, Min Li, Yuhong Wang
pmc-11375557.description: Metastasis is the leading cause of mortality in patients with malignant tumors, particularly characterized by peritoneal metastases originating from gastric, ovarian, and colorectal cancers. Regarded as the terminal phase of tumor progression, peritoneal metastasis presents limited therapeutic avenues and is associated with a dismal prognosis for patients.

pmc-11507503.title: Three-Stage Cascade Information Attenuation for Opinion Dynamics in Social Networks
pmc-11507503.creator: Haomin Wang, Youyuan Li, Jia Chen
pmc-11507503.description: In social network analysis, entropy quantifies the uncertainty or diversity of opinions, reflecting the complexity of opinion dynamics. To enhance the understanding of how opinions evolve, this study introduces a novel approach to modeling opinion dynamics in social networks by incorporating three-stage cascade information attenuation.

pmc-12551271.title: Engaging anaesthesia professionals as co-faculty in stroke thrombectomy simulation training: associations with clinical care and patient outcomes
pmc-12551271.creator: Caroline Guldberg Fugelli, Hege Langli Ersdal, Soffien Ajmi, Jan Terje Kvaløy, Lars Fjetland, Cecilie Grøtteland, Snorre Eikeland, Victoria Brazil, Martin Wilhelm Kurz
pmc-12551271.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundSimulation-based training for endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) may improve care for patients with acute ischaemic stroke. This study investigated whether engaging anaesthesia professionals as co-faculty in an established in situ simulation programme influenced EVT care and patient outcomes.MethodsThis single centre pre-post interventional study (2017-2023) evaluated the impact of revising an EVT simulation training programme by engaging anaesthesia professionals in its design, delivery, and debriefing.

pmc-12686494.title: Analytical and numerical solutions of MABC fractional advection dispersion models by utilizing the modified physics informed neural networks with impacts of fractional derivative
pmc-12686494.creator: Emad A Az-Zo’bi, Adel S Hussain, Mujahid Iqbal, Abeer Aljohani, Mohammad A Tashtoush, Nahaa E Alsubaie, Firas K A Al-Hamarneh, Nazar Mohammad Nazar, Dumitru Baleanu
pmc-12686494.description: Transport of pollutants is a serious environmental concern, where accurate and effective mathematical models are essential for developing viable mitigation programs. In this work, this study proposes new formulation of advection dispersion equations of fractional order and employ them to model the highly complex advection dispersion phenomena.

pmc-13253189.title: Comparative analysis of physiological, biochemical and immunological responses to heat stress in hybrid and purebred ducks in tropical environments
pmc-13253189.creator: Md Abu Hemayet, Md Sazedul Karim Sarker, Zulkifli Bin Idrus, Md Zulfekar Ali, Awis Qurni Sazili, Mohammad Shamsul Alam Bhuyian, Halima Khatun, Dela Ayu Lestari, Asep Setiaji, Mamat Hamidi Kamalludin
pmc-13253189.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Heat stress is a major environmental constraint compromising poultry productivity, welfare, and health in tropical regions. This study evaluated the adaptive responses of five duck genotypes, including local Rupali, a BLRI-improved common duck with white plumage; Pekin, an exotic duck; F1, a crossbred (two-way crossing: Pekin ♂ x Rupali ♀); Muscovy duck, an exotic and H1, the first hybrid (three-way crossing: Muscovy ♂ x Pekin ♂ x Rupali ♀) under heat stress in tropical Bangladesh.

pmc-13300094.title: Regular Aerobic Exercise Can Effectively Ameliorate the Skeletal Muscle and Mitochondrial Function Impairments Caused by bves Deficiency in Zebrafish
pmc-13300094.creator: Wanwan Cai, Wanbang Zhou, Xiushan Wu, Junrong Lei, Haochen Wang, Qiong Wu, Song Zhou, Kang Sun, Xiuyan Li, Zhilong Zhang, Jisheng Zhang, Jingying Ouyang, Yongqing Li, Zhigang Jiang, Xianchu Liu, Wuzhou Yuan, Lan Zheng
pmc-13300094.description: The Popeye domain-containing protein 1 (Popdc1), also known as Bves, plays a crucial role in maintaining skeletal muscle homeostasis, with its variants leading to limb–girdle muscular dystrophy type R25. Skeletal muscles of patients with the homozygous missense variant of Bves exhibit impaired membrane trafficking, while skeletal muscle fibers in bvesS191F homozygous mutant zebrafish are significantly reduced and disorganized.
